According to the text, after 1500 cycles at 1C, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS capacity per gram of sulfur. 

The text also states that the cathode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), which is the capacity per gram of the whole electrode.

The sulfur share of the electrode is 35 wt%, as stated in the text.

To find the ratio of capacity per gram of sulfur to capacity per gram of the whole electrode, we can divide the capacity per gram of sulfur by the capacity per gram of the whole electrode:

306 mAh/gS / 87 mAh/g = 3.52

This ratio implies that the cathode delivers approximately 3.52 times more capacity per gram of sulfur than per gram of the whole electrode.

The ratio of the sulfur share of the electrode (35 wt%) to the ratio of capacities (3.52) is:

35 wt% / 3.52 = 9.93%

This means that the sulfur share of the electrode is approximately 9.93% of the capacity ratio, which is lower than the stated sulfur content of 35 wt%.
